org: U.S. Department of Energy, Solar Energy Technologies Office (now listed under the Integrated Energy Systems Office)
program_hint: Solar funding notices: past agrivoltaics calls FARMS and SolWEB2, and any new solar notice
why: DOE solar office has funded agrivoltaics research directly (FARMS, SolWEB2) and a 2026 DOE environmental review covers an award to the University of Arizona for agrivoltaic treatments, so check for the next call.

org: National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL), InSPIRE agrivoltaics project
program_hint: InSPIRE research partnership and affiliated research network
why: DOE-funded national research network on solar with agriculture that lists partnership opportunities; a way into DOE agrivoltaics money as a field-site partner, so check whether it offers subawards.

org: U.S. Department of Energy SBIR/STTR (Office of Technology Commercialization)
program_hint: DOE SBIR/STTR Phase I and II releases (reauthorized April 2026)
why: STTR funds a small business together with a university research partner on clean energy topics, which fits a UA plus AVS or YPV team; confirm which 2026 topics name solar with agriculture.

org: USDA National Institute of Food and Agriculture, SBIR/STTR
program_hint: NIFA SBIR/STTR Phase I and II (reauthorized April 2026)
why: Funds small businesses with a research-institution partner to develop agricultural technology, so a UA plus company team could take an agrivoltaics tool or crop system to market.

program_hint: NSF SBIR/STTR Phase I and II
why: Funds small-business research and development with an optional university partner under STTR, a possible route for a company-led agrivoltaics or agricultural technology project with UA.

org: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Indian Energy Policy and Programs
program_hint: Unleashing Tribal Energy Development and Tribal Energy Capacity Expansion
why: Pays tribes for community-scale energy deployment and planning (USD 250,000 and up per award in 2026) and tribal colleges can apply, so UA could join as a technical partner on solar for rural and farming communities.

org: NOAA Climate Program Office, Climate Adaptation Partnerships (formerly RISA)
program_hint: Climate Adaptation Partnerships regional team competition (FY2026 closed June 2026)
why: UA already hosts the Southwest team (CLIMAS) funded by this program, so SALSAV could join as a partner on heat and drought adaptation for Southwest agriculture.

org: National Science Foundation, Advanced Technological Education (ATE)
program_hint: NSF 24-584 ATE, annual proposals due first Thursday in October
why: Funds technician training in fields like solar and agricultural technology, led by two-year colleges with university partners, so a SALSAV workforce curriculum with a community college could fit.

org: U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Desalination and Water Purification Research Program
program_hint: DWPR Research Funding Opportunity (2026 round: up to USD 5.7 million, closed Sept 29, 2026)
why: Recurring federal funding for lab and pilot research on treating brackish and impaired water, which links to irrigation water and energy use in the Southwest.

org: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service, Regional Conservation Partnership Program
program_hint: RCPP Classic and Alternative Funding Arrangements (FY2026 round closed Aug 2026)
why: Large partner-led conservation awards where higher education institutions are eligible partners, a way to fund an agrivoltaics water and soil demonstration with growers and a lead partner.

org: USDA National Institute of Food and Agriculture, Organic Agriculture Research and Extension Initiative (OREI)
program_hint: OREI Research Projects with Extension and/or Education Components (FY2026 round closed May 14, 2026)
why: Annual grants of up to USD 3.5 million for research and extension with land-grant universities, useful if SALSAV trials run on organic or transition land.

org: National Science Foundation, Translation to Practice (NSF TTP)
program_hint: NSF 25-540 TTP-E, TTP-T and TTP-P tracks (up to USD 600,000 to 2 million)
why: Pays university teams to move research results into real-world use with a partner, a possible next step for SALSAV findings if an NSF award already exists.

org: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, Food for Progress
program_hint: Food for Progress Program NOFO (FY2026 round closed July 6, 2026)
why: Annual multi-year awards to universities and nonprofits for agricultural productivity abroad; the 2026 countries were outside SALSAV sites, so watch the FY2027 country list for Latin America or Africa.

org: Desert Southwest Cooperative Ecosystem Studies Unit (hosted by the University of Arizona)
program_hint: Federal agency research agreements through the CESU network (17.5% indirect cap)
why: UA-hosted network that lets federal land, water and conservation agencies fund university research on a fast agreement, a route for Arizona dryland and solar land-use projects.

org: National Alliance for Water Innovation (NAWI), DOE energy-water hub
program_hint: NAWI industrial water reuse RFP (2026: USD 12 million, full proposals due Nov 24, 2026) and later RFPs
why: DOE-funded hub that pays universities, labs and industry for energy-efficient water treatment and reuse pilots, an energy-water link to explore for farm and rural water.
